text:
maria: quick sync — i'm putting a short proposal in this thread for per-route consent/granularity for request/response captures. goal: let product teams pick safe defaults while giving platform/ent customers an opt-in path for deeper inspection.

maria: TL;DR: add `log_mode` (none | metadata | redacted | raw-optin), deterministic `sample_seed` per-route, and an `inspect_breakglass` role for ephemeral full-access. console exposes per-route toggle + org override.

kevin: do we have any rough numbers on cost/storage impact for metadata vs redacted vs raw-optin? need this for quota UI.

maria: quick back-of-envelope: metadata ~0.2KB/req, redacted ~1KB, raw ~3-8KB depending on payload. plan: show est per-100k requests in console and warn when enabling raw-optin.

sam: retention and auditability questions: if someone enables raw-optin, do we still retain for the shorter default retention with separate audit log flag? legal/scc wants explicit consent recorded.

maria: yes — raw-optin requires explicit org-level acceptance and writes an audit record with `consent_id` that references a signed consent token. retention for raw-optin will be configurable but defaults to 30d and must be approved by security.

jen: from a UX angle, default should be `redacted` for new routes. want the console flow to make the difference obvious: little modal explaining what raw-optin means + checkbox for org-admin and a cooldown. also need a canary toggle for dedicated customers.

kevin: how are we doing redaction technically? regexes are brittle. prefer fast-hash for identifiers + pattern detectors for emails/cc/ssn. also need to keep stable fingerprinting for debugging without storing raw.

maria: agreed. propose layered approach: 1) token-level masks for free-text using model-assisted PII detector, 2) deterministic hashing for stable ids, 3) optional structured field allowlist (org-managed) to preserve certain metadata.

maria: example route config (YAML):

```
route: /v1/completions
log_mode: redacted         # none | metadata | redacted | raw-optin
sample_seed: 42            # deterministic sampler seed (0-2^31)
sample_rate: 0.01         # fraction captured when sampling enabled
retain_days: 30
inspect_breakglass: true   # allows ephemeral full access via audit flow
allowlist_fields:
  - customer_id
  - feature_flag
```

kevin: for deterministic sampling — can we use `hash(request_id) % 1e6 < sample_rate*1e6` so it's stable across retries? also we need the ability to toggle sampling in the console without redeploy.

maria: yes — use request_id hash for determinism and respect `x-replay` for replayed requests. sampling decision stored in trace metadata so downstream workers know whether to attach full payload. console toggle maps to a per-route runtime flag in config store (no redeploy).

sam: we should defend against accidental PII leaks in logs and dumps (heap/core). add a policy to sanitize any request payloads that go into debug dumps. ops-oncall: will need a breakglass approval for dump retrieval.

maria: agreed — add server-side scrub for debug-dumps: apply `redact_policy` before any dump is persisted. dump retrieval triggers audit-bot which records `who, why, token`.

kevin: small implementation note: model-assisted PII detector will be async for perf; we should support two modes: `inline` (strict, adds latency) and `async` (best-effort, post-hoc redact + tombstone). prefer async with a fast inline fallback for obvious tokens (emails, ccn).

maria: plan: async detector + inline heuristics. if async detects residual PII in a record flagged as redacted, we rotate and replace the record with a tombstone and emit an incident to the audit log.

jen: console UX — show a per-route "privacy score" and an estimated cost delta. also add an "impact simulator" where you paste a sample request to see what fields would be redacted. legal likes this for approvals.

kevin: devex ask: SDKs should expose `console_sampling_id` header for deterministic sampling and `redact_hint` for structured fields. keep header names short.

maria: agreed — headers: `X-RW-SAMPLE-ID` and `X-RW-REDACT-HINT` (comma separated). document in SDK changelog.

sam: one edge-case: customer-side encryption. if request payloads are encrypted end-to-end, we cannot redact server-side. need a clear error and fallback (deny, metadata-only).

maria: note added: if payload is E2EE, route must be marked `metadata` or `none`. console should block enabling redacted/raw on E2EE routes and require a signed exception.

kevin: going to estimate dev work: server: sampling + gating (2 wks), PII detector infra + async pipeline (3 wks), console UI + simulator (2 wks), SDK headers + docs (1 wk). add QA and security review.

maria: rollout: stage 1 internal-only on dev env, stage 2 canary to 5 dedicated customers, stage 3 global opt-in UI. will run small telemetry evals and a quality regression suite against our prompt sets.

jen: i'll make the console design ticket and add the modal copy.

kevin: i'll open the infra RFC and include that hashing sampler snippet.

sam: sounds good. once RFC lands, i'll schedule the security review.

ops-bot: new rfc created: RFC-3854 (logging-consent-granularity). link: https://r.example/rfc/3854 :robot_face:

audit-bot: audit event recorded: rfc:create by maria at 2533332000

maria: thanks all — next step: kevin + i will pair on the infra RFC. comments welcome inline on RFC. :thumbsup:

kevin: +1, will ping infra-arch for review.

sam: :thumbsup:
